claims.statement: create_deep_agent is the primary entry point that constructs a fully configured deep agent, returning a compiled LangGraph graph with planning, filesystem, subagent, and summarization middleware bundled in.
The README quickstart constructs an agent with create_deep_agent(model, tools, system_prompt) and runs it with agent.invoke({"messages": ...}), the standard construct-then-invoke usage.
The model argument accepts either a provider:model string (resolved via init_chat_model) or a pre-initialized BaseChatModel instance.

The tools argument is additive: user tools are merged with the built-in suite (ls, read_file, write_file, edit_file, delete, glob, grep, execute, and task) and passing tools never removes a built-in tool.
The final system prompt is assembled as caller USER prompt first, then the active harness profile's BASE and SUFFIX appended (USER -> BASE -> SUFFIX).
create_deep_agent compiles into a create_agent graph and configures it with a very high recursion_limit of 9,999 so long-horizon tool-calling loops can take many steps.

Custom middleware is inserted after the base stack (skills, filesystem, subagents, summarization, patch-tool-calls) but before the tail stack (profile middleware, prompt caching, memory, human-in-the-loop), and a custom middleware whose name matches an existing entry replaces it in place.

subagents supports three forms — declarative SubAgent, pre-compiled CompiledSubAgent, and remote AsyncSubAgent — where SubAgent and CompiledSubAgent are exposed through the task tool and AsyncSubAgent (identified by graph_id) is routed into AsyncSubAgentMiddleware and run as a background task.

If no subagent named general-purpose is supplied, a default general-purpose synchronous subagent is auto-added unless the active harness profile disables it, and when no synchronous subagents remain the task tool is not exposed.

The filesystem and shell tools run against a pluggable backend that defaults to StateBackend, and the execute tool only runs shell commands when the backend implements SandboxBackendProtocol, otherwise returning an error.
skills= loads skill source paths on demand via SkillsMiddleware and memory= loads AGENTS.md-style files at startup via MemoryMiddleware, both surfacing content into the system prompt.

FilesystemMiddleware and SubAgentMiddleware are protected scaffolding that back the built-in file tools and the task tool handler respectively, and a harness profile cannot exclude them — attempting to do so raises ValueError.
Passing interrupt_on, or permissions rules with interrupt mode, auto-installs HumanInTheLoopMiddleware so specified tool calls pause for human approval.

A custom state_schema must be a TypedDict subclass of DeepAgentState so the built-in DeltaChannel reducer on messages is preserved, and defining state via middleware is preferred over a custom base schema.

checkpointer, store, context_schema, response_format, cache, name, and debug are passed through to create_agent/LangGraph for persistence, structured output, and run configuration rather than altering the harness behavior.

Deep Agents is an opinionated harness layered on top of LangChain's create_agent (itself on LangGraph), bundling filesystem, sub-agents, context management, and skills, and any LangGraph CompiledStateGraph can be plugged in as a sub-agent.
Passing model=None to create_deep_agent uses a deprecated fallback ChatAnthropic model and will no longer be supported in deepagents==1.0.0, so applications should construct a model explicitly.

Filesystem permissions are ordered first-match rules with allow, deny, and interrupt modes; they are enforced by FilesystemMiddleware for built-in filesystem tools rather than by direct backend access, and declarative subagents inherit them unless they specify replacement rules.

Interrupt-mode filesystem permissions are converted to path-aware HumanInTheLoopMiddleware predicates; explicit interrupt_on entries override generated entries with the same tool name, while bulk filesystem calls conservatively interrupt when their scope could intersect a protected path.

AsyncSubAgent connects through the LangGraph SDK to an Agent Protocol server and returns task identity immediately for tracked background work; an async parent entrypoint is required when using local ASGI transport without a URL.

The focused unit test suites test_graph.py and test_permissions.py respectively cover graph/profile assembly and filesystem permission/HITL behavior, and the project Makefile runs tests through uv with socket access disabled except Unix sockets.
StateBackend stores files in graph state, persists them within a conversation thread through checkpointing rather than across threads, and can only be accessed inside LangGraph execution.

LocalShellBackend implements SandboxBackendProtocol but executes shell commands directly on the local host without sandboxing, process isolation, or security restrictions; filesystem restrictions can be bypassed through shell access.

Memory sources are concatenated in source order, stripped of HTML comments before prompt injection, and the injected guidelines direct the model to treat memory as reference material rather than instructions that override user requests or verified evidence.

The end-to-end unit suite uses scripted fake chat models to verify that a deep agent can invoke built-in filesystem tools, invoke custom tools, and complete multiple sequential tool calls while returning the resulting message state.
